prompts: A client loves the woodblock print attached, also in {WS}/print.jpg; it is in the public domain. They want a 3D wallpaper that copies it: its composition, its palette and its subjects, so anyone who knows the print recognizes it at a glance, rebuilt as our own low poly scene with some gentle motion. Deliver {WS}/scene/index.html, a single file with everything built in code: the print is the reference, not a texture. Record in {WS}/result.json what you took from it: boats (how many the print shows) and mountain (its name). It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
**[goal]** Rebuild Hokusai's *The Great Wave off Kanagawa* as a single-file low-poly 3D wallpaper with gentle motion, plus a `result.json` recording what was taken from the print.

**[action]**
- Inspected `./print.jpg` visually: towering curling wave (left), snow-capped Fuji (right-center), three fishing boats, beige washi sky, indigo/white/vermilion palette.
- Wrote `./result.json` (boats: 3, mountain: Mount Fuji) and `./scene/index.html` — one file, all geometry built in code (no textures), loading only Three.js 0.170.0 from jsdelivr.
- Verified in a real browser (file:// URL): wave curls with a foam lip and hanging claws, Fuji reads with its snow cap, all three vermilion boats sit in the foreground, clouds drift upper-right.
- Closed the browser tabs I opened (none remain).

**[result]**
- `./scene/index.html` — renders correctly, no build step; only external fetch is the allowed Three.js CDN URL.
- `./result.json` — `{"boats": 3, "mountain": "Mount Fuji", ...}` with assumptions noted.
- Motion: wave swell/lean, rolling swells, bobbing boats, drifting clouds, shimmering mist.

**[evidence]** Two browser screenshots of the rendered file: first showed a spiky crest and hidden Fuji (fixed), final shows the curling wave, visible Fuji, and three visible boats matching the print's composition and palette.

**[assumptions stated]** The print is a reference, not a texture; palette sampled from the image (indigo blues, white foam, washi beige, vermilion hulls); "gentle motion" = slow wave/boat/cloud animation.

**[what I found / how I know it's right]** The print is Hokusai's *Kanagawa oki nami ura* (c. 1831, public domain) — identifiable by the claw-crested wave, the small snow-capped Fuji framed by the curl, and exactly three boats. I counted the boats directly in the image (left trough, center, right) and confirmed Fuji's identity from the title block and its distinctive conical snow cap. The scene reproduces those same elements in the same arrangement, so anyone who knows the print recognizes it at a glance.
